To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a procedure for measurement of mono- and sesqui- terpenes in serum and plasma of sheep is described; (b) this method was modified and extended for measurement of terpenes in rumen fluid; (c) the method was used to determine the concentrations of 14 terpenes in sheep serum, 15 terpenes in plasma and 13 terpenes in fluid from rumen after consumption of terpene-laced shrubs.

(1) The method described herein can be used to quantify terpene concentrations in sheep serum and rumen fluid; (2) This method is suitable for use with plasma; and (3) This method is not suitable for quantifying all terpenes in all fluids.
the modified procedure for measuring terpenes in sheep blood and rumen fluids is suitable for serum, plasma, or rumen fluid and can be used to measure a wide range of mono- and sesqui- terpenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of the consumption of essential oil rich plants on ruminants, with special emphasis on their potential to be used as natural feed additives.
the use of terpene-rich shrubs as a source of natural products to modify ruminal fermentation.
developing a procedure that allows for the measurement of structurally-diverse monoterpenes in both serum/plasma and rumen fluid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this procedure is useful for measurement of a number of monoterpen and sesquiterpens in serum, plasma and rumen fluid.
the procedure described in this study can be used to measure a number of structurally diverse terpenes in sheep serum, plasma, or rumen fluid.
this method is useful for the measurement of terpenes in serum and plasma but that it is not as useful for the measurement in rumen fluid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
terpene concentrations are not necessarily the same in plasma and serum, and the concentrations in serum and plasma are not necessarily the equal to those in rumen fluid.
the method is not suitable for the analysis of all terpenes in all matrices.
the procedure for measuring terpenes in sheep serum and plasma can be adapted to measure terpenes in rumen fluid, and vice versa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of plasma and serum is interchangeable for the quantitation of terpenes in small ruminants.
terpene recovery is highly dependent on both the structure and the fluid in which the terpenes are measured.

the use of solid phase extraction (SPE) with a C-18 column and a C-8 column in tandem, followed by GC-FID, is a suitable method for the analysis of terpenes in serum and plasma, but is less suitable for rumen fluid.
